title: Esau's Family Becomes the Nation Edom
overview: This chapter lists the families, clan chiefs and kings descended from Esau, Jacob's brother, whose people became the nation of Edom.

parts.label: Esau moves to Seir (vv. 1-8)
parts.note: Esau, also called Edom (meaning "red"), takes his large household to Seir, the hill country south of the Dead Sea, because he and Jacob have too many animals for one land. His wives' names differ from earlier chapters, which may mean they had two names or that different records were combined; no one is sure.

parts.label: Sons and clan chiefs (vv. 9-19)
parts.note: Esau's sons and grandsons became chiefs, meaning heads of clans much like tribal sheikhs. One grandson, Amalek, born to a secondary wife of lower status, founded a people who later became Israel's fierce enemy.

parts.label: The earlier people of Seir (vv. 20-30)
parts.note: The Horites lived in Seir before Esau's family, who married into them and, according to later books, eventually took over their land. The rare Hebrew word for what Anah found is uncertain: most modern translations say "hot springs," older ones say "mules."

parts.label: The kings of Edom (vv. 31-39)
parts.note: None of these eight kings is called the son of the king before him, and seven are linked to seven different places, which suggests the crown was not simply passed from father to son. The phrase "before any Israelite king" suggests to many scholars that this list was written down or updated after Israel had kings.

parts.label: Chiefs by region (vv. 40-43)
parts.note: A final list names Edom's chiefs by the places where their clans lived. Some names repeat earlier people, such as Timna and Oholibamah, perhaps because clans or districts were named after ancestors, though the link is unclear.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether this chapter mainly shows that Esau, though not the chosen line, was still blessed and given a land of his own, or mainly closes his story so the narrative can focus on Jacob's family.
think: When two siblings or old rivals go separate ways, can parting be a kind of peace, or is it always a loss?
